default.notes: San Marino has no border controls of its own — entry runs through Italy, so an Italian Schengen short-stay visa is required.

groups.notes: EU citizens enter through Italy with a passport or national ID card and may visit San Marino freely — there are no controls on the Italy–San Marino border.
EFTA citizens enjoy free movement through Italy equivalent to EU citizens and may visit San Marino freely.
Visa-free under Schengen rules, entering through Italy — 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen Area. ETIAS authorisation will be required once mandatory.
Visa-free with a biometric passport under Schengen rules, entering through Italy — 90 days in any 180-day period. ETIAS authorisation will be required once mandatory.
Visa-free with a biometric passport under Schengen rules, entering through Italy — 90 days in any 180-day period. ETIAS authorisation will be required once mandatory.

SM.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Sammarinese citizens.

UA.notes: Visa-free with a biometric passport under Schengen rules, entering through Italy — 90 days in any 180-day period.

RU.notes: A Schengen short-stay visa via Italy is required. The EU suspended its visa facilitation agreement with Russia; fees are higher (€90) and processing is slower.

VU.notes: The EU suspended Vanuatu's visa waiver over its citizenship-by-investment scheme; a Schengen short-stay visa via Italy is required.
